summary: Retire idle replication HTTP connections sooner and retry unanswered exchanges once on a fresh connection

replay.detail: No graph replay or admission-format change. A transport retry reuses the exact signed request body. Authentication has no nonce/timestamp window, active jobs reuse sender plus body digest, and duplicate envelope receipt is idempotent.

schema.detail: No persisted schema, state or migration.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules, digests or coordinated fleet upgrade.

compatibility.detail: The per-peer client idle pool deadline is ten seconds instead of reqwest's ninety-second default. An exchange transport failure before complete response headers receives one immediate attempt through a new private client. Application errors, HTTP statuses, response-body errors and other endpoints are not retried. Wire formats, signatures, compression negotiation and TCP keepalive settings remain unchanged.

downtime.detail: Each HTTP send retains its twenty-second timeout. Two stalled sends can therefore take forty seconds before route fallback or backoff, up to twenty seconds longer than before. The existing five-minute overload-poll deadline still cancels both sends; overload counts, delays and route cooldown policy are unchanged.

manual.detail: Normal binary upgrade; no configuration changes or production deployment performed.

recovery.detail: A stale pooled stream can recover immediately after its first failed send on a fresh TCP connection without re-exporting or re-signing the exchange. This locally reproduced failure mode is not a proven production root cause. Pre-extraction request-head and body-read diagnostics distinguish no head arrival from a stalled upload.
